categoryName: Men wear — innerwear, vests, tees, shirts, trousers, track, kurta-pyjama, socks

skuLines.line: Sikh kachhera — readymade cotton, elastic waist
skuLines.examples: local Ludhiana/Amritsar stitchers; 'Sikhi Kachhera' organic cotton (Amazon); Punjab hosiery house brands
skuLines.packSizes: single, pack of 2, pack of 3; sizes 26-44 waist + boys 20-28
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; spike at session start (Apr) and Vaisakhi
skuLines.notes: Non-negotiable at a Sikh institution — this is the single most under-stocked line in generic apparel planograms. Carry BOTH nada (drawstring) and elastic types; amritdhari staff and older students insist on nada. Local stitching keeps landed cost low; no national brand covers depth of sizes.

skuLines.line: Turban / dastar cloth — full voile, cut lengths
skuLines.examples: Madhurani, Charkhi, Moorni full voile; F74 rubia; malmal
skuLines.packSizes: cut to 5 m / 6 m / 8 m; also stitched-hemmed pieces
skuLines.priceBand: ₹250-900 per piece depending on metres and quality
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; big spike Gurpurab (Nov), Guru Gobind Singh Jayanti (Dec-Jan), Vaisakhi (Apr)
skuLines.notes: Sold by the metre — needs a cutting table, a metre rule and a hemming/singeing service, not just a shelf. Keep the institutional colours (navy, white, kesri/saffron, black, grey) in permanent depth; fashion shades are dead stock. Fabric line, so GST and HSN differ from readymade garments.

skuLines.examples: Sardar Pagri Hause patka; local stitchers; school-colour patka
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; peaks at session start and after each break
skuLines.notes: Highest-churn Sikh apparel item in a residential boys' school — they get lost, torn and outgrown. Must match the Academy's uniform colours; verify with the school before buying colour depth.

skuLines.examples: local; cotton keski; printed parna
skuLines.notes: Cheap, tiny, fast-moving; a counter-top basket item. Buys the trip that also picks up a kachhera.

skuLines.line: Men's white cotton vest, round neck sleeveless — mass
skuLines.examples: Lux Cozi, Dollar Lehar, Amul Macho, VIP, Dixcy Scott
skuLines.notes: The bread-and-butter line. Hostel laundry destroys these, so pack-of-3 white in every size, never single pieces. Stock local-mill unbranded alongside branded for the lowest price point — non-teaching staff buy on price.

skuLines.line: Men's premium combed-cotton vest, extended length
skuLines.examples: Jockey 8820, Jockey FP04, Dollar Bigboss
skuLines.notes: Teaching staff and faculty trade up; extended length for easy tuck under a shirt. Keep 1-2 SKUs only, this is a premium shoulder not a volume line.

skuLines.examples: Bodycare, Dollar Champion, Lux Venus, Rupa Frontline Junior
skuLines.seasonality: peaks Apr session start; steady all year
skuLines.notes: Sizing by chest-cm not age — carry the full ladder or wardens buy off-campus in bulk. Name-tape or marker service attaches directly to this line.

skuLines.line: Coloured / gym vest — muscle fit, racerback, elastane
skuLines.examples: Jockey 9930 muscle vest, TECHNOSPORT, XYXX, DaMENSCH
skuLines.notes: University-age gym demand. Grey, black, navy only; bright colours sit.

skuLines.line: Winter inner vest — full sleeve, cotton-wool blend
skuLines.examples: Lux Cottswool, Rupa Thermocot, Dollar Ultra Thermal, Oswal
skuLines.notes: Baru Sahib sits high enough that this is a survival item, not a comfort one. Must be on shelf BEFORE the first cold snap — a stockout in November sends every wallet to Rajgarh/Solan.

skuLines.examples: Lux Cottswool set, Rupa Thermocot, Oswal Inner Set, HEATEK fleece thermal
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Feb; single sharpest seasonal peak in the whole category
skuLines.notes: Pre-book in Aug-Sep — mills allot on early orders and hill retailers who indent in October get nothing. Carry a cheap cotton tier AND a fleece-lined tier; keep boys' sizes too. Season carry-over risk: unsold thermals dead-stock until next October, so buy to a hard number.

skuLines.examples: Amul Macho, VIP Frenchie, Dollar Bigboss, Dixcy Scott, Lux Venus
skuLines.notes: Volume driver. White + assorted. Note many residents wear kachhera instead — do not over-index on briefs at the expense of kachhera depth.

skuLines.line: Men's premium combed-cotton brief, ultrasoft waistband
skuLines.examples: Jockey 8035, Jockey 8037, Jockey US59
skuLines.notes: Jockey is the trade-up brand every Indian store needs one facing of. Concealed vs exposed waistband are two different buyers.

skuLines.examples: Jockey 8008/8009 long trunk, Lux Cozi Bigshot, XYXX Aero, Jockey FP23 printed
skuLines.notes: Trunks have overtaken briefs for under-30s across India — this is where university demand actually sits. Solid + printed both move.

skuLines.examples: XYXX Uno micromodal, DaMENSCH, Ethika Airsoft, Jockey IC28 Tactel
skuLines.notes: Thin premium tail — 2-3 SKUs maximum. Justifies its shelf only because there is no alternative shop for 50 km; a faculty member who wants this today has nowhere else.

skuLines.line: Woven boxer shorts with pockets — lounge crossover
skuLines.examples: Jockey US57, Symbol printed boxers, DaMENSCH Bermuda
skuLines.notes: Doubles as hostel/quarters loungewear, so it sells to two occasions. Pockets are the deciding feature.

skuLines.examples: Jockey M100/M101 Marvel Avengers, Bodycare, Dollar Champion
skuLines.seasonality: peaks Apr and after each break
skuLines.notes: Licensed prints command a premium the school-age cohort actually pays. Size ladder matters more than print variety.

skuLines.examples: traditional cotton langot; sports supporter with pouch
skuLines.notes: Two distinct demands hide behind one SKU: kabaddi/wrestling/PT use, and post-hernia/hydrocele support for older staff. Nowhere else within 50 km sells it. Very low stock value, disproportionate goodwill.

skuLines.line: Sports compression base layer — top and tights
skuLines.examples: TECHNOSPORT, Boldfit, Nivia, Decathlon-equivalent
skuLines.notes: Only worth stocking if the Academy runs competitive teams — check with the sports department before buying, otherwise it dead-stocks.

skuLines.line: Round-neck plain cotton T-shirt — mass, 160-180 GSM
skuLines.examples: Symbol (Amazon private label equivalent), Lux Cozi, local mill PC tees
skuLines.notes: Highest-margin volume line in the whole category. Solid colours in white, black, navy, grey, maroon. Buy a shallow colour range and deep sizes, never the reverse.

skuLines.examples: Jockey 2714/2715, Levi's 025, Allen Solly, True Classic
skuLines.notes: A branded facing anchors price perception for the whole tee bay.

skuLines.line: Printed / graphic tee — oversized, drop shoulder
skuLines.examples: AUSK baggy hip-hop tee, ColorChakra oversized, BULLMER printed pack, Lymio
skuLines.notes: The clearest 2026 shift in Indian menswear. But screen a Sikh institution's sensitivities on slogans and imagery — buy plain-graphic and typographic, avoid anything with alcohol, tobacco, or provocative artwork.

skuLines.examples: Lux Cozi polo (mass), Peter England, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Louis Philippe (premium)
skuLines.notes: The default smart-casual for teaching and admin staff; also the shape most used for institutional/departmental t-shirts. Carry both price tiers — the gap between ₹399 and ₹999 is exactly the staff-grade gap.

skuLines.examples: Peter England, Symbol formal, Allen Solly, Van Heusen
skuLines.seasonality: session start, convocation, annual function, interviews
skuLines.notes: White and light blue are 60% of demand. Neck-size ladder is the whole job — a shop with only S/M/L loses the sale.

skuLines.examples: Allen Solly casual, U TURN, DEELMO, local Ludhiana makes
skuLines.notes: Plus sizes (XXL-4XL) are chronically under-bought in small-town India and non-teaching staff need them.

skuLines.examples: DEELMO linen, Zilcon, Louis Philippe
skuLines.notes: Thin tail; 2-3 options. Creases badly, which hill customers dislike — sample before committing.

skuLines.examples: QUTUN waffle henley, NETCLICK half-open collar, Beyoung
skuLines.notes: New shape trending in 2025-26; works as a mid-layer in a cold campus, which gives it a real function here rather than only fashion.

skuLines.examples: Alan Jones zipper hoodie, Lymio, Scott International, Allen Solly crew sweatshirt, Mack Jonney half-zip
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Mar; the biggest winter unit-mover after socks
skuLines.notes: On a cold residential campus a hoodie is worn over the uniform daily. Plain navy/black/grey outsell prints. Bulky — plan freight and shelf cube; hill road transport charges by volume, not weight.

skuLines.line: Half-zip fleece pullover / polar fleece top
skuLines.examples: Mack Jonney half-zip, The Modern Soul, Boldfit fleece
skuLines.notes: The 2026 replacement for the woollen sweater in this price band — lighter, cheaper, machine washable, which matters where hostel laundry is communal.

skuLines.examples: Peter England knit super trouser, Symbol formal, Mc Henry, SaintX, The Pant Project
skuLines.notes: Stretch/lycra waistband is now the default expectation, not a premium feature. Stock unhemmed or offer free hemming — length is the number-one reason a trouser sale fails in a small store.

skuLines.examples: Symbol chinos, Louis Philippe chinos, Mehrang slim chino
skuLines.notes: Beige, navy, olive, black. Bridges formal and casual, so it covers a staff member who owns one pair of trousers.

skuLines.examples: Wrogn loose fit, Urbano Fashion, Levi's, local Ludhiana denim
skuLines.notes: Slow-turning, high-value, size-fragmented — the classic small-store inventory trap. Two fits, three washes, deep middle sizes only; let the rest be a special-order/indent item.

skuLines.examples: Lymio cargo, Vogaan cargo, GRECIILOOKS lycra cargo, Samfor utility
skuLines.notes: Strongest-selling casual bottom for the 18-25 cohort in 2025-26. Drawstring waist forgives sizing, which is exactly what a small store needs.

skuLines.line: Track pants — cotton / PC, side pockets
skuLines.examples: Jockey 9500, Symbol knit track pants, Lymio TP series, Alan Jones joggers, RynoGear
skuLines.notes: On a residential campus with compulsory PT this is a daily-wear bottom, not sportswear. Navy and black in deep sizes; the school's PT colour is the SKU that actually sells — confirm it.

skuLines.examples: Alan Jones French terry jogger, BE SAVAGE 320 GSM heavyweight, FN3 relax fit, O3e
skuLines.notes: Heavyweight 300+ GSM is a genuine 2026 trend AND genuinely warmer — the rare case where fashion and hill function agree.

skuLines.line: Track suit set — jacket + jogger, fleece
skuLines.examples: SKM fleece tracksuit, GLAMY, Scott International, local fleece sets
skuLines.notes: High ticket, bulky, colour-and-size fragmented. Best handled as an indent/pre-book against the sports department or hostel wardens rather than open stock.

skuLines.examples: KART BLACK knee-length shorts, Symbol, DHRIVANSH cargo shorts, Boldfit
skuLines.notes: Hostel/quarters wear more than outdoor wear. Modesty matters at a Sikh institution — buy knee-length, not short-inseam athletic.

skuLines.line: Pyjama — cotton, checked and solid, elastic waist
skuLines.examples: Jockey 9009 checkered, XYXX Checkmate, Symbol cotton pyjama, Majestic Man, SleepZ by Raymond
skuLines.packSizes: single; pack of 2/3; S-XXL, plus one-size elasticated
skuLines.notes: Universal across every cohort including elderly staff. Side pockets and a real drawstring (not just elastic) are what older buyers check. Stock a warm flannel/hosiery-thick version for winter separately.

skuLines.line: Lounge pants / night pant and night-suit set
skuLines.examples: U.S. Polo Assn. lounge pants, XYXX pyjama, Vogaan tee+shorts night set, DIGITAL SHOPEE pack of 3
skuLines.notes: Married-staff-quarters demand. Sets sell better than separates as gifts around Diwali/Bandi Chhor Divas.

skuLines.line: Kurta — cotton, short and long, mandarin collar
skuLines.examples: Majestic Man, ROYALSCOUT, Symbol cotton kurta, Zombom, DEELMO
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurab (Nov), Guru Gobind Singh Jayanti (Dec-Jan), Hola Mohalla (Mar), Vaisakhi (Apr), Diwali/Bandi Chhor (Oct-Nov)
skuLines.notes: White and off-white are the institutional colours and must never be out of stock during a Gurpurab week. Both short kurta (daily/casual) and long kurta (kirtan/darbar) are needed — they are two different buys.

skuLines.examples: DIVISIVE cotton-linen kurta pyjama, SleepZ by Raymond kurta set, Majestic Man, local Punjabi makes
skuLines.seasonality: sharp peaks at every Gurpurab and Vaisakhi; also weddings Nov-Feb
skuLines.notes: The one apparel line where a stockout is socially visible. Pre-position 4-6 weeks before each Gurpurab. White, cream, and light pastels only; heavy sequins and zari move poorly in a monastic-institution setting.

skuLines.examples: Majestic Man Nehru jacket, local makes, Amazon Symbol
skuLines.notes: Low turns but high visibility on the institution's own function days. 3-4 sizes in navy/black/cream is enough.

skuLines.examples: cotton / cotton-linen suiting-shirting by the metre; Amazon 'Unstitched Fabric' category equivalents
skuLines.packSizes: 2.5 m kurta piece, 2.5 m pyjama piece, or 5 m sets
skuLines.notes: Older residents and anyone hard to fit still get kurta-pyjama tailored. Only worth carrying if a tailoring service (own or tie-up) is attached — otherwise it is inert.

skuLines.examples: SWAGR pack of 12, Fitness Mantra 12-pair, SJeware pack of 5, Supersox
skuLines.notes: Highest-margin, highest-frequency line in the category and almost impossible to over-stock — socks disappear in hostel laundry. 12-pair bulk packs are the single best value proposition for a residential student.

skuLines.examples: Peter England cotton socks, Supersox calf-length office socks, Jockey 7036
skuLines.notes: Black, navy, dark grey. Pairs with the formal-trouser buyer at the same till.

skuLines.line: School uniform socks — white/grey with stripe
skuLines.examples: Bonjour school socks, Supersox school range, local makes
skuLines.seasonality: peaks Apr and after every break
skuLines.notes: Must match the Academy's exact stripe/colour spec — get the specification in writing from the school before indenting, or the whole buy is unsellable.

skuLines.examples: Balenzia winter socks, Supersox thermal, Heelium, merino crew packs
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Mar; sells out first every winter in hill towns
skuLines.notes: For a cold, damp hill campus this is a health item — cold feet in a hostel is the complaint that drives a trip to town. Buy deeper than instinct says; terry-cushion and full-wool are two different price tiers, carry both.

skuLines.examples: Heelium bamboo ankle socks, Balenzia bamboo, Supersox anti-odor
skuLines.notes: Genuine 2025-26 growth pocket in Indian hosiery. One facing only.

skuLines.examples: SWAGR sports crew, Adidas/Puma ankle 3-pack, Nivia
skuLines.notes: Football/athletics teams buy in bulk — worth a standing quote to the sports department.

skuLines.line: Belt — leather / vegan leather, autolock and pin buckle
skuLines.examples: ZORO leather belt, Labnoft autolock, Peter England, local nylon fabric belt
skuLines.notes: Cuttable/autolock belts collapse the size problem to one SKU — the right choice for a single-store assortment. Black and brown; plus a plain black school belt for uniform.

skuLines.examples: Bombay Dyeing, Peter England, local cotton hankies
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; spikes in cold and allergy season
skuLines.notes: Trivial value, near-zero risk, constant demand — a counter-basket line, and the only handkerchief source for 50 km.

skuLines.line: Muffler / scarf and woollen cap (monkey cap, beanie)
skuLines.examples: Balenzia muffler, DIKHAWA scarf, PAROPKAR cotton-lycra skull cap, local Ludhiana woollens
skuLines.notes: May belong to a separate winter-accessories lane, but function-critical here. Note headwear must work over/under a turban or patka for Sikh residents — a beanie that does not fit a patka wearer is dead stock; skull-cap/keski-compatible styles and mufflers sell instead.

skuLines.examples: AWG All Weather Gear, Scott International polyester jacket, Lymio lightweight jacket, Duckback rainwear
skuLines.seasonality: Jun-Sep monsoon; also Oct-Mar as a windbreaker
skuLines.notes: Sirmaur monsoon is heavy — this is the item residents currently buy off-campus. Packable hooded styles beat bulky ones for hostel storage. Sits at the boundary with an outerwear lane, but should not be left unowned.

skuLines.line: Boys' school uniform shirt and trouser
skuLines.examples: Enterprise school uniform, Yellow Bee, local uniform stitchers
skuLines.packSizes: single; age/size 4-16, half and full trouser
skuLines.seasonality: Apr session start; replacement all year
skuLines.notes: Flagged: this likely belongs to a kids/uniform lane, but if ARY is the only shop the school's uniform must be sourced somewhere. Requires the Academy's written spec (shade, collar, pleats, house colours) and is best run as a fixed-price institutional line, possibly billed to the student account rather than cash.

skuLines.line: Sewing notions — nada/drawstring, elastic, buttons, name tapes
skuLines.examples: cotton nada, 1-inch braided elastic by the metre, shirt-button cards, printed name tapes
skuLines.packSizes: per piece / per metre / card of 12
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; name tapes peak in April
skuLines.notes: The invisible line that makes a residential-campus apparel bay work: every kachhera and pyjama needs a nada, every hostel garment needs a name tape, and a snapped elastic otherwise means a 50 km trip. Almost no working capital, very high margin.

trends2026: Trunks have displaced briefs as the default under-30 innerwear shape — Amazon India's men's innerwear bestseller list is now dominated by trunks and long trunks (Jockey 8008/8009, Lux Cozi Bigshot, XYXX Aero), with briefs holding on mainly at the mass end.

Fabric and feature claims have gone mainstream at ₹500-1,000: micromodal, antimicrobial/antibacterial, 'no-marks' waistband, moisture-move and 4-way stretch now appear on the majority of bestselling and new-release innerwear SKUs (XYXX Uno, DaMENSCH, Ethika Airsoft, Jockey Tactel).

Heavyweight and oversized has become a real spec, not a style word — 300-320 GSM baggy track pants and drop-shoulder oversized tees are among Amazon India's fastest new releases, which happens to also be warmer and therefore genuinely useful in a hill campus.

Stretch has become the default in formal bottoms: nearly every bestselling formal trouser now advertises lycra/knit 'super trouser' 360-degree stretch or an expandable/techno-flex waistband, and non-stretch formal trousers are getting hard to sell.

Fleece has largely replaced the woollen sweater in the ₹500-1,300 winter band — half-zip fleece pullovers, fleece hoodies and fleece tracksuit co-ord sets now carry the winter top business, being cheaper, lighter and machine-washable.

Sock premiumisation: bamboo, merino and anti-odour/antibacterial socks are a visible new tier above plain cotton, sitting alongside 12-pair bulk value packs at the other extreme — the middle is thinning.

Men's shapewear and compression vests have crossed from niche to bestseller-list presence (XYXX Sculpt, YADIFEN, Yadifen-type tummy tuckers), a category that did not exist in Indian mass retail three years ago.

Plus-size availability is now advertised on the product itself ('Available in Plus Sizes' appears across Amazon's own Symbol label and most fast-growing sellers) — carrying only S-XL is now read as an incomplete assortment.

GST 2.0 (effective 22 September 2025) collapsed India's slabs toward 5% and 18%; the apparel threshold has been widely reported as 5% up to ₹2,500 per piece and 18% above, which if correct pulls almost this entire assortment into the 5% band. Confidence: moderate — the two-rate reform and its date are confirmed, the ₹2,500 apparel cut-off is not, so verify with the accountant before repricing.
Co-ord sets (matching top + bottom, sold as one decision) are absorbing share from separates in loungewear and casualwear, which simplifies buying for a small store but raises the size-matching risk.
adjacentServices: In-house or tie-up tailoring: trouser hemming and waist alteration — the single highest-conversion service in a store with no second option nearby, and the fix for the length problem that kills trouser sales.
Turban-cloth cutting, hemming and singeing at the counter, with a metre rule and standard 5/6/8 m cut lengths.
Name-tape printing and stitching / permanent marker service for hostel garments (vests, socks, shirts, track pants) — attaches to almost every student purchase in April.
Repair and mending desk: zip replacement, button re-stitch, nada and elastic replacement, small tears. Turns a 50 km trip into a ₹30 counter transaction.
Size-measure and indent/special-order for odd sizes (waist 44+, chest 48+, XXL-5XL, unusual shoe-linked sock sizes) with a promised delivery date on the next inbound truck.

Seasonal pre-book: take thermal, woollen sock and fleece orders from hostel wardens and departments in August-September, indent against the confirmed number, and avoid both the November stockout and the March dead stock.
Institutional bulk supply against the school/university account: PT track pants, house t-shirts, uniform socks, sports socks, quoted per unit and billed to the department rather than the individual.
Exchange and size-swap window (7-10 days, tags intact) — the trust mechanism a captive-market store needs so residents are willing to buy apparel locally instead of waiting for a town trip.
Laundry and pressing / dry-clean collection point for staff quarters, using the same counter and the same weekly vehicle.
Festival pre-order for kurta-pyjama and white kurta ahead of each Gurpurab and Vaisakhi, taken 4-6 weeks out with a small token advance.
